finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the query parameter f is joined to /srv/files with filepath.Join, which cleans '..' but does not confine the result to the root. An unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary files readable by the process, such as /etc/passwd.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: name taken from the attacker-controlled query string with no validation
file contents returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No prefix or containment check on the joined path, no filepath.Base, no allowlist, and no authentication or authorization middleware. Handler is registered directly on the default mux at files.go:32. Repro: GET /dl?f=../../etc/passwd. The avatar handler at files.go:22 uses filepath.Base and is not vulnerable.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the unvalidated query param f to os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("/srv/files", name)) with no containment, Base, or auth check, so ../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd and is written out at files.go:18, while the /avatar handler (files.go:22) is protected by filepath.Base.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query param f straight into filepath.Join("/srv/files", name) and os.ReadFile, with no containment check or auth, so ../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd and is written at files.go:18 (the handler is registered at files.go:32).
